text.p: CardioThoracic Systems Inc said on Wednesday Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp had chosen CardioThoracic as its preferred partner to provide products and training for minimally invasive bypass surgery.

CardioThoracic said it would train Columbia-affiliated surgeons to use its MIDCAB System, a set of minimally invasive direct coronary artery bypass instruments designed to facilitate surgery performed on a beating heart.
Columbia/HCA is the largest U.S. provider of healthcare services, based in Nashville, Tenn.
Richard Scott, chairman and chief executive of Columbia, said: "We believe minimally invasive bypass surgery can improve long-term patient outcomes and potentially revolutionize cardiac surgery."

The MIDCAB procedure let surgeons, through a three-inch to four-inch incision between the ribs, access and bypass a diseased artery using the internal mammary artery or other suitable vascular graft, CardioThoracic said.
Under the deal, CardioThoracic said it would customize its training program to instruct cardiac surgeons at Columbia/HCA's 95 cardiac surgery centers on how to use the MIDCAB System.
The companies would also create a clinical patient registry database to track short- and long-term results and to document the system's cost-effectiveness, CardioThoracic said.
